Rashi on Gittin 42b:10:1.hebrew: הפיל - רבו שינו של עבד כנעני, ואח"כ סימא את עינו:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:10:1.english: Knocked out - his master [knocked out] the tooth of a Canaanite slave, and afterward blinded his eye:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:10:2.hebrew: יוצא בשינו - לחירות, וקס"ד צריך גט שחרור, וכי סימא עינו קודם גט, נותן לו דמי עינו כבן חורין:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:10:2.english: He goes out due to his tooth - to freedom; and it is currently assumed [that] he requires a bill of manumission, and [yet] when [the master] blinded his eye before [giving] the bill [of manumission], he gives him the value of his eye as [for] a freeman.

Rashi on Gittin 42b:11:1.hebrew: בכולן - עשרים וארבעה ראשי אברים האמורין במס' נגעים (פ"ו מ"ז) לענין שאינן מטמאין משום מחיה: ראשי אצבעות של ידים ורגלים, וראש החוטם, וראשי האזנים, וראש הגוויה — שהן משופעין לכאן ולכאן, ואין נגען נראה לכהן בבת אחת, ולא קרינא ביה "לכל מראה עיני הכהן" (ויקרא י״ג:י״ב):
Rashi on Gittin 42b:11:1.english: For all of them - [This refers to] the twenty-four extremities of limbs mentioned in Tractate Negaim (6:7) with regard to [the law] that they do not become ritually impure due to healthy flesh [appearing in a leprous lesion]: the tips of the fingers and toes, the tip of the nose, the tips of the ears, and the tip of the male member — for they slope to one side and the other, so their lesion is not visible to the priest all at once, and we cannot apply to it [the verse], "wherever the eyes of the priest look" (Leviticus 13:12).

Rashi on Gittin 42b:11:2.hebrew: עבד יוצא בהן לחירות - דמומין שבגלוי הן ואינן חוזרין כשן ועין, ואתרבו בכלל ופרט וכלל בפ"ק דקדושין (דף כד:):
Rashi on Gittin 42b:11:2.english: A slave goes out to freedom by means of them - For they are exposed blemishes that do not heal [lit., return], like a tooth and an eye, and they were included [in this law] through a generalization, a specification, and a generalization in the first chapter of Kiddushin (24b):

Rashi on Gittin 42b:12:1.hebrew: המכריעין - דעת חכמים איזו נראה, ולא אתפרש מאן נינהו:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:12:1.english: Those who decide - [regarding] the opinion of the Sages, which one appears [correct], and it is not explained who they are:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:13:1.english: But don't we interpret verses - In Kiddushin (ibid.):

Rashi on Gittin 42b:14:1.english: He partakes of teruma - if he is the slave of a priest:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:14:2.english: "The purchase of his money," the Merciful One states - regarding terumah:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:15:1.hebrew: אוכלין בתרומה - שניהם ממה נפשך, דחד כהן וחד עבד כהן:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:15:1.english: [They] may partake of terumah - both of them, either way, for one is a priest and one is the slave of a priest:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:15:2.hebrew: וחולקין חלק א' - ביבמות (דף צט:) מפרשים: חלק כאחד, שאין נותנין להם תרומה בגורן לזה בלא זה; דקסבר אין חולקין תרומה לעבד כנעני בגורן אלא א"כ רבו עמו, דלמא אתי למימר "כהן הוא" ומסקו ליה ליוחסין, והשתא לא אתי לאסוקינהו; והאי מעוכב גט שחרור הוא, ואין לרבו רשות עליו דלא ידע הי מינייהו עבד, וצריכין שישחררו זה את זה; וקתני סיפא "הגדילו התערובות, משחררין זה את זה", וקתני "אוכלין בתרומה":
Rashi on Gittin 42b:15:2.english: And they divide one portion - In Yevamot (99b) they explain [this to mean] one portion together, for they do not give them terumah at the threshing floor to one without the other; for [the Tanna] holds [that] one does not distribute terumah to a Canaanite slave at the threshing floor unless his master is with him, lest [people] come to say, "He is a priest," and elevate him to [priestly] lineage, whereas now [when both appear together, people] will not come to elevate them. And this [slave] is one who lacks a bill of manumission, and his master has no authority over him, since he does not know which of them is the slave, and they need to emancipate one another; and the latter clause teaches, "When the mixed [children] grow up, they emancipate one another," and [yet] it teaches, "they may partake of terumah":

Rashi on Gittin 42b:17:1.english: Whose master sold him - to another [person]:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:17:2.hebrew: לקנס - שאם יגחנו שור יהא קנסו שלו, אבל לשאר דברים לא מכרו:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:17:2.english: With regard to the penalty - [Meaning] that if an ox gores him, his penalty will belong to him [the buyer], but for other matters he did not sell him:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:17:3.english: [Is he] sold - at least with regard to the penalty:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:17:4.hebrew: או לא מכור - ואם נגח, קנסו לרבו ראשון, דאין אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:17:4.english: Or [is he] not sold - And if [an ox] gored [him], his penalty [belongs] to his first master, because a person cannot transfer ownership of something that has not yet come into the world:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:18:1.hebrew: תיבעי לר"מ - דאמר אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם, כגון האומר לאשה: "הרי את מקודשת לי לכשאתגייר כו'" (קדושין דף סג.):
Rashi on Gittin 42b:18:1.english: Raise the dilemma according to Rabbi Meir - who says that a person can transfer ownership of an entity that has not yet come into the world, [such as] one who says to a woman, "Behold, you are betrothed to me when I convert," etc. (Kiddushin 63a):

Rashi on Gittin 42b:18:2.hebrew: פירות דקל - המוכר פירות דקל עד שלא חנטו, דפליגי בה רב הונא ורב נחמן אליבא דר' מאיר:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:18:2.english: Produce of a date palm - [This refers to] one who sells the produce of a date palm before they have budded, regarding which Rav Huna and Rav Nachman disagree according to Rabbi Meir:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:1:1.english: And half of a ransom - [for] the aspect of freedom:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:1:2.hebrew: ליורשיו - ולקמן פריך: יורשין מנא ליה:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:1:2.english: To his heirs - And later on, [the Gemara] asks: From where does he [have] heirs?

Rashi on Gittin 42b:2:2.hebrew: וסופה לחזור - ושיימינן ליה כמה דמיו פחותים בכך למכור עכשיו בשוק, ואם יום של רבו היה, ינתן הכל לרבו, ואם יום של עצמו היה, הכל לעצמו:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:2:2.english: And it will eventually return - And we assess for him how much his value is diminished thereby to sell [him] now in the market; and if it was his master's day, everything is given to his master, and if it was his own day, everything [goes] to himself:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:3:1.hebrew: הניחא לאביי - דאמר בב"ק (דף פו.) באדם שחבל בחברו בענין זה:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:3:1.english: This works out well according to Abaye - who said in Bava Kamma (86a) regarding a person who injured his fellow in this manner:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:3:2.hebrew: נותן לו שבת גדולה ושבת קטנה - שבת גדולה — הן פחת דמיו לימכר עכשיו בשוק, והוא נזק. ולהכי קרי ליה שבת, שפחת דמיו של עכשיו אינו אלא משום שבת, שאינו ראוי לעשות מלאכה בשתי ידיו עד זמן שתחזור ידו, אלא לשמור קישואים יהא ראוי לאחר שיקל ממנו כאב המכה קצת. ושבת קטנה — היינו כאילו הוא שומר קישואין, שנותן לו כל ימי חליו שישכב במטה מחמת חולי זה, שאינו יכול לשמור קישואים:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:3:2.english: He gives him [for] major loss of livelihood and minor loss of livelihood - Major loss of livelihood — this is the depreciation in his value [if he were] to be sold now in the market, and it is [considered] damages. And for this reason he calls it "loss of livelihood" [shevet], because the depreciation in his value now is only on account of loss of livelihood, as he is not fit to perform work with both of his hands until the time his hand recovers; rather, he will be fit [only] to guard cucumbers after the pain of the blow subsides somewhat for him. And minor loss of livelihood — this is [assessed] as if he were a cucumber watchman, as he pays him [for] all the days of his illness that he lies in bed on account of this illness, when he is unable [even] to guard cucumbers:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:3:3.hebrew: שפיר - דכיון דשייך דין נזק במכה זו, מיחייב שור עלה, וכיון דלא כליא קרנא לגמרי, יום של רבו לרבו, יום של עצמו לעצמו:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:3:3.english: [This works out] well - For since the law of damage [payment] applies to this injury, an ox is liable for it; and since the principal [value] is not completely destroyed, his master's day [goes] to his master, [and] his own day [goes] to himself:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:4:1.hebrew: שבתו של כל יום ויום - ואין כאן פחת דמים, הואיל וסופו לחזור, אלא לפי שבת של כל יום יתן לו: כל ימי נפילתו למטה יתן שכר אדם שלם לפי מלאכה שהיה רגיל בה, וכשיעמוד ויהא ראוי לשמור קישואין — ישמור קישואין, וזה יתן לו פחת השכר:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:4:1.english: His loss of livelihood for each and every day - And there is no [payment for] depreciation in value here, since he will eventually recover; rather, he pays him according to the loss of livelihood of each day: all the days he is confined to bed, he pays the wage of a healthy person according to the work to which he was accustomed; and when he gets up and becomes fit to guard cucumbers, he guards cucumbers, and this one [the injurer] pays him the difference in wages:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:4:2.hebrew: האי שור הוא - כלומר, הואיל ואדם החובל כך אינו משלם נזק אלא שבת, שור פטור לגמרי, דה' דברים גבי אדם כתיב ולא גבי שור, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ד:י״ט): "איש כי יתן מום בעמיתו" — ולא שור בעמיתו:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:4:2.english: This [case] is an ox - That is to say, since a person who injures [someone] in this manner does not pay [for] damage, [but] rather [only for] loss of livelihood, an ox is completely exempt, for the five [categories of] payments are written regarding a person and not regarding an ox, as it is written (Leviticus 24:19): "If a man inflicts a blemish upon his fellow" — and not an ox upon his fellow.

Rashi on Gittin 42b:5:1.hebrew: איבעית אימא - הא דאמרן לעיל "יום של רבו לרבו", מיירי כשהכהו אדם:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:5:1.english: If you wish, say - [Regarding] that which we said above, "[payment for] his master's day [goes] to his master," [this refers to a case] where a person struck him:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:5:2.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - לעולם בשור, וכאביי דאמר שייך בה דין נזק, ודקמקשית מינה לרבא:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:5:2.english: And if you wish, say - Actually, [it is speaking] of an ox, and in accordance with Abaye, who said [that] the law of damages applies to it; and as for that which you objected from it against Rava:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:5:3.hebrew: הך מימרא - בעלמא היא, ואינה לא משנה ולא ברייתא:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:5:3.english: This meimra - is merely [an amoraic statement], and it is neither a Mishnah nor a Baraita:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:5:4.hebrew: ומימרא - רבא אמר לך דהא מימרא לא ס"ל:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:5:4.english: And a statement - Rava [would] say to you that he does not hold of this statement:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:6:1.hebrew: מעוכב גט שחרור - מחוסר גט שחרור — כל הנך דאמרי' בהו דיצאו לחירות ואין לרבו עליהם כלום אלא שצריכין גט שחרור, כגון מקדיש ומפקיר, ומי שחציו בן חורין דתנן "כופין את רבו":
Rashi on Gittin 42b:6:1.english: Detained [by] a bill of manumission - Lacking a bill of manumission — [referring to] all those [slaves] regarding whom we say that they have gone out to freedom, and their master has [no claim] over them except that they require a bill of manumission, such as [when a master] consecrates or declares [his slave] ownerless, or one who is half-free, [regarding] whom we learned [in a Mishnah]: "We compel his master [to free him]:"

Rashi on Gittin 42b:6:2.hebrew: יש לו קנס - שלשים כסף לרבו, אם נגחו שור:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:6:2.english: [Does] he have a penalty - [Namely,] thirty silver [shekels] to his master, if an ox gored him:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:8:1.hebrew: מאי לאו כמשנה אחרונה - לאחר שחזרו בית הלל להורות דכופין את רבו, ואפי' הכי שקיל קנס דצד עבדות כל זמן שלא נכתב הגט:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:8:1.english: What, is [it] not in accordance with the ultimate [version of the] Mishnah - [meaning] after Beit Hillel retracted [their earlier ruling] to rule that we force his master [to emancipate him], and even so he collects the penalty for the slave portion as long as the bill [of manumission] has not been written:

Rashi on Gittin 42b:9:1.hebrew: כמשנה ראשונה - דלית ליה כופין, ואדון גמור הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 42b:9:1.english: In accordance with the initial version of the Mishnah - which does not hold [that] we force [the master to emancipate him], and he is a full master:

Tosafot on Gittin 42b:10:1.hebrew: חבלי ביה אחריני יהבי ליה לרביה - אע"ג דמעשה ידיו לעצמו, כיון דקנסא לרבו, חבלה נמי לרבו, דמה לי קטליה כולו ומה לי קטליה פלגא:
Tosafot on Gittin 42b:10:1.english: If others injure him, they give [it] to his master - Even though his handiwork belongs to himself, since the penalty goes to his master, [payment for] injury also goes to his master; for what is the difference to me [whether] he killed him completely or killed him partially:

Tosafot on Gittin 42b:13:1.hebrew: הואיל ומדרש חכמים הוא - אומר ר"ת דחיישי' שמא ימצאנו בשוק ויאמר לו "עבדי אתה", אבל בשן ועין לא חיישי', ד"זיל קרי בי רב" הוא:
Tosafot on Gittin 42b:13:1.english: Since it is an interpretation of the Sages - Rabbeinu Tam says that we are concerned lest [the master] find him in the market and say to him, "You are my slave"; but regarding a tooth or an eye, we are not concerned, because it is [a matter of] "go read [it] in the schoolhouse" [i.e., universally known from Scripture]:

Tosafot on Gittin 42b:14:1.hebrew: מעוכב גט שחרור אוכל כו' - הך בעיא לא אתיא אליבא דר"ל דריש פרק בתרא דכריתות (כד:), דמסקינן אליבא דרשב"ג דמעוכב גט שחרור אוכל בתרומה. אי נמי יש לחלק, דהתם במעוכב גט שחרור ע"י הפקר אוכל בתרומה, כמו שמותר בשפחה כדפרישית לעיל, והכא איירי בחציו עבד וחציו בן חורין:
Tosafot on Gittin 42b:14:1.english: One detained [without] a bill of manumission, may he partake, etc. - This dilemma does not follow the opinion of Reish Lakish at the beginning of the last chapter of Keritot (24b), where we conclude according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel that one detained [without] a bill of manumission may partake of terumah. Alternatively, one can distinguish: there, regarding one detained [without] a bill of manumission through renunciation of ownership, he may partake of terumah, just as he is permitted [to marry] a slavewoman, as I explained above; whereas here, [the Gemara] is speaking of one who is half-slave and half-free:

Tosafot on Gittin 42b:15:1.hebrew: הרי אלו אוכלים בתרומה - והא דאמרינן בפ"ק דכתובות (דף יג:) גבי עשרה כהנים ופי' אחד מהם ובעל, הולד שתוקי, שמשתיקין אותו מדין כהונה, מדכתיב "והיתה לו ולזרעו אחריו", שיהא זרעו מיוחס אחריו — הא אמרינן בפ' נושאין על האנוסה (יבמות דף ק:) דזרעו מיוחס אחריו דרבנן, וכי גזור רבנן בזנות, בנישואין לא גזרו. אי נמי, הכא לאחר שנולדו נתערבו:
Tosafot on Gittin 42b:15:1.english: These may partake of teruma - And [as for] that which we say in the first chapter of Ketubot (13b) regarding ten priests, where one of them separated [from the group] and cohabited [with a woman]: the child is a shetuki, whom we silence from the status of priesthood, as it is written, "And it shall be for him and for his seed after him" — [teaching] that his seed must be traced after him — we say in the chapter [entitled] Nos'in al Ha'anusa (Yevamot 100b) that [the requirement that] "his seed be traced after him" is rabbinic; and when the Rabbis decreed [this], [it was] in [a case of] licentiousness, [whereas] in [a case of] marriage they did not decree [it]. Alternatively, here they became mixed up after they were born:

Tosafot on Gittin 42b:17:1.hebrew: עבד שמכרו רבו לקנס כו' - מכר קנס של עבד לא מיבעיא ליה, דאפי' לר"מ לא קני, דהא לא עבידי דאתי כדקאמרי', וכ"ש לרבנן. אלא במכרו רבו לקנס מיבעיא ליה: דדילמא אפי' לרבנן קני להו כמו דקל לפירותיו, כדאמרי' "הא קאי שור והא קאי עבד"; או דלמא אפי' לר"מ לא קני, דלא דמי [לפירות דקל], שהפירות יוצאים מגוף הדקל ועבידי דאתו, אבל קנסא מעלמא אתי ולא עבידי דאתי:
Tosafot on Gittin 42b:17:1.english: A slave whose master sold him with regard to the penalty, etc. - Selling the penalty of a slave [by itself] was not a dilemma for [the Gemara], for even according to Rabbi Meir [the buyer] does not acquire [it], since it is not likely to come [about], as [the Gemara] says [below], and all the more so according to the Rabbis. Rather, [the case] where "his master sold him with regard to the penalty" was a dilemma for it: for perhaps even according to the Rabbis he acquires it, like [one who sells] a palm tree for its fruit, as [the Gemara] says, "Here stands the ox and here stands the slave"; or perhaps even according to Rabbi Meir he does not acquire [it], for it is not similar [to the fruit of a palm tree], since the fruit emerges from the body of the palm tree and is likely to come [about], whereas the penalty comes from an external source and is not likely to come [about]:

Tosafot on Gittin 42b:4:1.hebrew: ושור אינו משלם אלא נזק - יש רוצים לפטור את השוכר או שואל סוס מחבירו, אפי' הוזק בפשיעה ונתבטל הרבה ממלאכתו, כיון דסופו לחזור להתרפאות, דכי היכי דדרשינן "איש בעמיתו" ולא שור בעמיתו, ה"נ דרשינן "איש בעמיתו" ולא איש בשור. ואין לחלק בין שומרים לאדם המזיק, מדפריך בב"ק (דף ד:): "ותו, שומר חנם והשואל כו'" — אדם דאזיק שור הוא. והא דפריך בריש הנחנקין (סנהדרין פד:): "הכחישה באבנים ה"נ דלא מיחייב" — היינו בהכחשה דלא הדרא. ור"ח אומר דלא שייך שבת אלא באדם, דשבתו לא הוי בכלל נזק, דמשום שבת לא פחתי דמיו כל כך; אבל שור — פשיטא דשבתו בכלל נזק הוא, דפחתי דמיו, ומתחלה כשהוזק שמין אותו כמה דמיו פחותים לימכר:
Tosafot on Gittin 42b:4:1.english: And an ox pays only damage - There are those who wish to exempt one who rents or borrows a horse from his fellow, even if it was injured through negligence and was idle from its work for a long time, since it will eventually heal [and return to health]; for just as we expound [the verse] "[If] a man [causes a blemish] in his fellow" [as teaching:] and not an ox [that injures] his fellow, so too we expound "a man in his fellow" [as teaching:] and not a man [who injures] an ox. And one cannot distinguish between bailees and a person who [directly] causes damage, [as proven] from that which [the Gemara] asks in Bava Kamma (4b): "Furthermore, an unpaid bailee and a borrower, etc." — [for that is a case of] a person who damaged an ox! And as for that which [the Gemara] asks at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Hanechnakin (Sanhedrin 84b): "[If] he weakened it with stones, so too is he exempt?!" — that is [speaking] of a weakening from which it does not recover. And Rabbeinu Ḥananel says that [a separate payment for] loss of livelihood applies only to a human being, whose loss of livelihood is not included in [the assessment of] damage, because on account of loss of livelihood his value does not decrease so much; but [for] an ox — it is obvious that its loss of livelihood is included in [the assessment of] damage, for its value does decrease, and from the outset when it is injured, we appraise how much its value has decreased for sale:

Tosafot on Gittin 42b:8:1.hebrew: מאי לאו כמשנה אחרונה - ולעיל לא בעי לאוקומי הא דנותן חצי קנס לרבו למשנה אחרונה, דקנסא לרבו, מעשה ידיו לעצמו; והא דנגחו שור יום של רבו לרבו, הוי למשנה ראשונה, כדפרישית לעיל, כי היכי דלא לפשוט בעיא דהכא:
Tosafot on Gittin 42b:8:1.english: What, is it not in accordance with the ultimate version of the Mishnah - And earlier, [the Gemara] did not want to establish that [statement] that "[the owner of the ox] gives half of a penalty to his master" according to the ultimate version of the Mishnah — that the penalty [goes] to his master [even though] his earnings [belong] to himself — while that [statement] that "if an ox gored him [on] his master's day, [it goes] to his master" is according to the initial version of the Mishnah, as I explained earlier, in order not to resolve the dilemma here:
